blocks.text: Reverend Josiah Olufemi Akindayomi, founder of the Redeemed Christian Church of God, was born on 5 July 1909 at Odo-Alafia Street, Ondo State, Nigeria. He married Pastor (Mrs) Esther Egbedire Akindayomi, and the two moved to Lagos in 1941, marrying that same year at the C&S Church.

Hungry for a deeper, more authentic walk with God, Reverend Akindayomi and his wife left the C&S Church in 1952 and started the Ogo Oluwa Society - a small fellowship that met weekly for prayer, worship, and Bible study. It was through this study of Scripture that they encountered the biblical teaching on restitution; Reverend Akindayomi, who had married three wives before this point, was led by the Holy Spirit to resolve the matter by retaining only his first wife.

cards.heading: A name given in a vision

blocks.text: As a man devoted to prayer, Reverend Akindayomi received the name "The Redeemed Christian Church of God" in a vision, and the Holy Spirit enabled him to write it down. The Ogo Oluwa Society took up this divinely revealed name as its banner. He was also given the assurance that the church would reach to the ends of the earth, and that the Lord Jesus Himself would meet the church at His second coming.
Reverend Akindayomi passed on to glory on 2 November 1980.

In March 1981, Pastor Enoch Adejare Adeboye - at the time a PhD holder in Applied Mathematics and a Senior Lecturer at the University of Ilorin - was divinely chosen to take over as General Overseer, inheriting a total of forty parishes.
Under his leadership, the church has experienced phenomenal growth, expanding to a presence in over 100 countries. To God be the glory.
